discovery: Photonic crystals: the photonic band gap and the control of light emission and propagation in periodic dielectric structures
motivation: In 1987 Yablonovitch and John independently proposed that periodic dielectric structures could exhibit a complete photonic band gap, forbidding light propagation in all directions. Yablonovitch showed this would suppress spontaneous emission; John showed it would localise light and create bound atom-photon states. Yablonovitch then realised the first three-dimensional band-gap material. Noda turned the concept into practice: full 3D band-gap crystals at optical wavelengths, ultrahigh-Q nanocavities, direct control of spontaneous emission, and photonic-crystal surface-emitting lasers, which are now commercial high-power sources. Photonic band-gap engineering gave physics a new way to shape the electromagnetic vacuum. It underpins solid-state cavity quantum electrodynamics with single quantum dots and colour centres, slow light, photonic-crystal fibres, topological photonics and integrated nanophotonics. Few concepts in optics have been as fundamental or as widely used as tools.
